claim: NVIDIA Dynamo offers a 'GAIE with vanilla vLLM' topology that adds Dynamo's KV-cache-aware routing to upstream vLLM pods without migrating them to the Dynamo worker stack, via a standalone Dynamo EPP doing direct vLLM worker discovery and vLLM-native token rendering.
stance_target: EPP-based routing to non-native (non-Dynamo-worker) backend fleets is an established, productized pattern outside llm-d/GIE
scope_conditions: NVIDIA Dynamo on Kubernetes, GAIE routing topology
quoted_support: Using GAIE with vanilla vLLM | You already run upstream vLLM pods and want to add Dynamo's advanced KV-aware routing without migrating the fleet to Dynamo workers. | Gateway API, GAIE, a compatible Gateway implementation, and standalone Dynamo EPP support. | EPP with direct vLLM worker discovery and vLLM token rendering.

claim: Dynamo's docs state worker-selection authority must be singular per request path: the Frontend must not re-select a worker after the EPP has already made the selection.
stance_target: design constraint for layering custom routing logic on top of EPP-based selection: only one component may own the pick per request
quoted_support: The Frontend and GAIE topologies are alternatives for a request path. Do not configure the Frontend to select a worker after the EPP has already selected one.

claim: In Dynamo's GAIE topology, worker Frontend sidecars run in --router-mode direct because routing decisions are already made upstream by the EPP, meaning the worker-side component trusts the externally selected destination rather than re-scoring it.
stance_target: pattern of downstream components trusting an EPP-selected destination without re-validation, applicable to non-pod backend routing designs
quoted_support: A Kubernetes Gateway receives the request and asks the Dynamo Endpoint Picker Plugin (EPP) to select an endpoint before forwarding the request to a worker pod... worker Frontend sidecars run with --router-mode direct because the EPP has already made the routing decision.
